sentences.text: This Civil Revision Petition is filed seeking a direction to the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal /
Small Causes Court at Chennai to take on file M.C.O.P.SR.No.8507 of 2022 filed by the petitioner and proceed in accordance with law.

2. The petition filed by the petitioner, seeking compensation in respect of injuries sustained in the motor accident that had occurred on 20.04.2022 has been returned by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal / Small Causes Court, Chennai on the ground that the petition is barred by limitation as per the amendments relating to the Motor Accident Claims which came into force on 01.04.2022.

entities.text: Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal / Small Causes Court, Chennai
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Aggrieved by the same, the present revision petition is filed.
3. Considering the limited relief sought for, notice to the respondents is deemed unnecessary.

4. The learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that as per the decision rendered in A.S.Krishnan Vs. Najeeb and Others [OP(MAC) https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis No.6 of 2023 decided on 23.01.2023] of the High Court of Kerala at Ernakulam, his claim petition should not be returned on the ground of limitation.

entities.text: A.S.Krishnan Vs. Najeeb and Others [OP(MAC) https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis No.6 of 2023
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: High Court of Kerala at Ernakulam
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
In this regard, it is relevant to extract para 24 of the said decision, which reads as follows :
24.As a fall out of my findings, the impugned orders are set aside, it is held that the provisions of the Limitation Act would be applicable for entertaining the petitions for claiming the compensation even beyond the period of six months, for, by taking into consideration, Rule 17 of Annexure XIII framed under Rule 150A of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules 1989, the limitation to entertain the claim petition cannot be restricted to six (6) months as there is no provision in the Act excluding the applicability of provisions of Section 29(2) of the Limitation Act.
In other words, it is held that the claim petitions, if filed beyond the period of six months cannot be dismissed in limine.

5. Considering the same, the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal / Small Causes Court, Chennai, is directed to consider the claim petition filed by the petitioner in M.C.O.P.SR.No.8507 of 2022 afresh,
taking into consideration of the decision rendered by the High Court of Kerala https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis at Ernakulam and pass appropriate orders, on merits and in accordance with law.

entities.text: Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal / Small Causes Court, Chennai
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 6. This Civil Revision Petition is disposed of at the admission stage itself, with the above observation and direction.
No costs.
7. The Registry is directed to return the original application to the petitioner, enabling the petitioner to represent the same before the Tribunal.
